# Operating the Machine

## Operator Workflow

This page describes the procedure followed by the user, from the digital pattern to the running prototype.

### 1. Create the Pattern

Create a three-colour PNG file with the [Pattern Editor](pattern-editor.qmd). The pattern must be 48 pixels wide and contain exactly three RGB colours.

### 2. Copy the Pattern to the USB Drive

Copy one or more `.png` files directly into the root folder of the USB flash drive.

### 3. Prepare the Hardware

Before starting a real test, verify that:

- the Raspberry Pi is powered;
- the ESP32 is connected to the Raspberry Pi through its USB cable;
- the three servomotors are supplied by the external regulated 5 V power supply;
- the DC-DC ground and the ESP32 ground are connected;
- the printed servo arms can move freely;
- the microswitch is connected to the ESP32.

See [Wiring and Power Supply](wiring-power.qmd) for the complete connections.

### 4. Start the Application

Mount the USB flash drive and run the integrated interface:

```bash
source /home/aless/venvs/uncinetto/bin/activate
sudo mount /dev/sda1 /mnt/pattern_usb
python3 /home/aless/gfxhat_pattern_ui_usb.py --usb-dir /mnt/pattern_usb --port /dev/ttyUSB0
```

### 5. Select the PNG from the Display

The display shows the files available on the USB drive:

```text
SELEZIONA PNG
> pattern_01.png
  pattern_02.png
  pattern_03.png
^v SPOSTA  OK SEL  + REF
```

Use:

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| `UP` / `DOWN` | Browse PNG files |
| `SELECT` | Confirm the selected pattern |
| `PLUS` | Refresh the file list |

### 6. Insert the Yarns

After file selection, the display shows:

```text
PATTERN SELEZIONATO
pattern_01.png

INSERIRE
I FILATI

+ AVVIA    < MENU
```

Place the three yarns consistently with the colour-to-servo mapping generated by the Raspberry Pi.

### 7. Start Production

Press `PLUS` (`AVVIA`). The Raspberry Pi validates the PNG, opens the USB serial communication with the ESP32 and immediately sends the command corresponding to the first pixel.

### 8. Monitor the Process

While the system is running, the display shows:

```text
pattern_01.png
IN LAVORAZIONE

[ progress bar ]

36%   18/50
- STOP
```

Every press of the synchronization microswitch causes the ESP32 to send `NEXT` to the Raspberry Pi. The Raspberry Pi then updates the percentage and sends the command for the following pixel.

### 9. Pause and Resume

During processing:

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| `MINUS` | Pause the process and move all servo arms to `DOWN` |
| `PLUS` | Resume from the preserved pixel |
| `BACK` | Return to the file-selection menu from the stopped screen |

### 10. Completion

At the end of the pattern, all servos are moved to their inactive position and the display shows:

```text
LAVORO
COMPLETATO

[ 100% ]

OK / < MENU
```

## Current Limitation

The current stop/resume implementation acts on the three colour-selection servomotors. Control of an additional main stepper drive is planned but is not part of the tested actuation firmware yet.
